channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: What TRON Swap Energy Pays For—and How You Cover It
item.description: TRON swap Energy pays for smart-contract execution. Staking, delegation, TRX burns and contract settings determine who covers a swap’s resource cost.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Transfer Is Stuck. Which Step Failed?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer can pause at confirmation, routing, liquidity or destination execution; check each stage in order before retrying or sending funds again.

item.title: Why a Swap Can Stay Pending: Tick Arrays Explained
item.description: Tick arrays supply ranges a concentrated-liquidity swap can cross; a bad sequence can fail execution, while network confirmation determines how long it stays pending.

item.title: Why a Native Bridge Withdrawal Can Take Days
item.description: Native bridge withdrawals wait for a chain’s exit proof and security window to clear; the delay depends on the rollup design, then a final claim releases funds.

item.title: How to Find Wallets Buying Near Local Lows
item.description: Finding wallets that buy near local lows means matching swap records to price turns, then checking whether those addresses held or quickly sold what they acquired.

item.title: TRON Swap: Where a Token Blacklist Stops Settlement
item.description: A TRON swap settles through token-contract transfers, so a blacklist can stop USDT at a specific address without freezing TRX or every asset on the network.

item.title: Why Treasury Swaps on TRON Leave Token Dust
item.description: TRON swaps can leave small balances when route sizing, token-unit rounding and treasury buffers do not align; tracing the route shows where the remainder sits.

item.title: Why Your XMR Deposit Is Pending and When to Retry
item.description: A pending XMR deposit may still be unconfirmed, waiting for the service to credit it, or hidden by a wallet that has not synced; check each stage before retrying.

item.title: How to Use zerofi When an XMR Transfer Stalls
item.description: A stalled XMR send can be a wallet, node or confirmation issue. Check its transaction ID and status before retrying to avoid creating a second payment.

item.title: How to Reconcile Cross-Chain Treasury Transfers
item.description: Cross-chain treasury transfers reconcile by matching a source-chain debit to a destination-chain credit, then resolving fees, delays and failures before closing the books.

item.title: Keep ETH and POL Ready for Polygon Bridge Transfers
item.description: Keep the right native token on each side of a Polygon bridge: ETH for Ethereum transactions and POL for Polygon PoS, including later withdrawal steps.

item.title: Why tiny token balances can get stuck on the bridge
item.description: A tiny balance can sit on Polygon yet fail to return because bridge routes, gas, minimums and token support all shape whether a withdrawal can proceed.

item.title: Paying a Team on Their Preferred Chains
item.description: Paying a team across chains means matching each wallet, token and fee path before sending; a clear payout policy prevents avoidable swaps and failed transfers.

item.title: Before Using Omnichain, Check Message Security, Time and Fees
item.description: An omnichain transfer depends on verified messages, destination finality and costs at both ends; check each layer before moving assets or application state.

item.title: What a Cross-Chain Bridge Quote Leaves Out
item.description: A bridge quote combines network gas, bridge fees and swap costs in different ways. Learn what to check before signing and how to compare routes fairly.

item.title: What an Intermediate Asset Means in a Treasury Route
item.description: A cross-chain treasury route may pass through an asset it never meant to hold; trace each leg, token form and accounting role before judging the result.

item.title: When Splitting a Cross-Chain Swap Pays
item.description: Splitting a cross-chain swap can improve the received amount when routes have different marginal costs, but extra fees and delay can erase the gain.

item.title: Why BSC Pair Choice Comes Down to Liquidity or Recency
item.description: On BSC, choose a trading pair by matching pool depth to your trade, then use recency to judge whether its price and activity still reflect current demand.

item.title: Why BSC Swap Quotes Change With Trade Size
item.description: A BSC swap quote changes with trade size because larger trades consume more pool reserves, increasing price impact alongside fees and any routing costs.

item.title: Mantle withdrawals: fast inclusion, slower Ethereum settlement
item.description: Mantle withdrawals can appear on the rollup quickly, while Ethereum settlement waits for proof, a challenge window and a final claim; that shapes when funds are usable.
